summary: Claude Code, given the multi-step auth feature request, loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, inspected the repo, wrote a design spec (docs only), then loaded the writing-plans skill — all before any implementation code was written.
reasoning: The authoritative session log shows the writing-plans skill was loaded after only read-only exploration plus a design spec markdown and a .gitignore — no implementation code preceded it. The scenario ends once planning starts, which it did.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch vs. the story: the acceptance criterion names `superpowers:writing-plans` but the agent loaded `hyperpowers:writing-plans` (and `hyperpowers:brainstorming`). Treated as equivalent/renamed plugin, but flagging in case the namespace matters.
The agent wrote a .gitignore containing both `docs/superpowers` and `docs/hyperpowers`, suggesting leftover/dual naming in the skill instructions.
Spinner label read 'Coalescing…' for 2m+ with no tool detail on screen; only the session log showed real progress.
Onboarding required 4 interactive confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) despite the launcher being described as pre-seeded with dialog-bypass state.
Prompt supplied by the story contains 'extreemly' (intentional per story text); agent handled it fine.
